source_review.notes: Reviewed Bayer-McCreight, Lehman-Yao, both Graefe publications, the cited textbook, current PostgreSQL nbtree design and insertion source plus PostgreSQL 18 B-tree documentation, and current official SQLite B-tree/atomic-commit material. Seven online primary or official destinations returned HTTP 200. The Microsoft Graefe PDF and ACM DOI destination returned automated-access HTTP 403; their primary metadata remained research-index readable. Product-specific behavior is explicitly version/current-source scoped.

evidence: Checked complete physical order <I, half-open page ranges, used/capacity/min occupancy, right-min pivots, height h, split levels s, merge levels m, WAL bytes W, and dirty pages D.
Checked that logical deletion, physical entry deletion, structural unlink, retirement, and reclamation are distinct terms throughout.
Checked stable-model terms against DBE-031's right-child-minimum convention and DBE-032's upper-bound descent.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Entry-count capacity is confined to the explicitly bounded fixed-width teaching model; production occupancy claims use encoded bytes and policy.

evidence: Independently recomputed insert 20 as leaves (5,10)|(15,20), pivot 15, and insert 30 as three leaves with pivots 15,25.
Independently recomputed delete 30 as merge-left to (5,10)|(15,20,25), pivot 15.
Independently recomputed delete 5 as borrow-right to (10,15)|(20,25), repairing the pivot to 20.
Independently recomputed delete 10 as merge-right and root shrink to the single root leaf (15,20,25).
Recomputed the variable-width counterexample: 24 entries per side can encode to approximately 3.84 KiB versus 1.76 KiB before metadata.
numerical_recomputation.notes: A separate reference trace using a different implementation printed independent_trace=True.

evidence: Re-derived right-min parent pivot repair for both left-to-right and right-to-left redistribution.
Re-derived split separation: all left keys <I p, all right keys >=I p, with complete original-range coverage.
Re-derived root growth/shrink preservation of uniform leaf depth.
Re-derived the stable-state induction over no-repair insert/delete, split, redistribution, merge, recursive parent repair, and root exception.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The stable proof assumes a correct complete comparator and declared separator representation; it does not establish a production concurrency or recovery theorem.

evidence: Reviewed empty/root-leaf tree, root exception, first root split, cascading internal/root split, unary-root shrink, absent deletion, and minimum siblings unable to lend.
Reviewed maximum/variable-width encodings, duplicate runs, total tie-breakers, prefix/suffix-truncated pivots, posting lists, collations, NULLs, and split-boundary equality.
Reviewed concurrent stale descent, repeated right correction, parent publication lag, latch ordering/restart, incomplete split, half-dead/unlinked page, pin/epoch/generation protection, and reuse.
Reviewed crash boundaries before/after split WAL and parent/root publication, repeated redo, independent dirty-page flush, and stale incarnation rejection.
Reviewed monotone hot edge, random-key scattering, split/merge oscillation, cleanup debt, cancellation/resource bounds, and telemetry cardinality.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Allowed transient states must be named by a concrete engine protocol; the chapter does not universalize PostgreSQL state names.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status for the executable model.
The model validates nonempty bounded leaves, maximum/minimum occupancy with root exception, globally sorted distinct keys, exact separator/right-child minima, and child/separator arity.
Manual review checked complete reachability, uniform depth, high-key/right-link publication, parent repair, no premature reuse, and allocation/orphan/leak obligations beyond the bounded model.

Draft structural checks accepted front matter, required section order, ten distinct examples, five exercises, five matching answers, local links, and executable snippet expectations before stopping only for this review record.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable model is single-threaded, in-memory, fixed-width, distinct-key, and limited to one internal root; omitted domains are explicit in the chapter.

evidence: Reviewed the induction base and every structural mutation case for sorted membership, range partition, exact routing, and leaf-depth preservation.
Reviewed the safety argument for right-reachable split publication before parent completion against the cited B-link protocol.
Reviewed why redistribution changes the parent pivot and merge removes exactly one child relationship.
Reviewed all five exercise answers for trace correctness, representation assumptions, crash-state interpretation, policy trade-offs, and evidence limits.
proof_review.notes: No proof of linearizability, deadlock/starvation freedom, serializability, WAL implementation correctness, reclamation safety, or universal performance is claimed.

evidence: The stable-state induction is explicitly labeled a proof sketch and its assumptions/omissions immediately follow it.
The executable artifact is repeatedly labeled a bounded teaching model rather than a production protocol.
PostgreSQL is used as a scoped implementation example, while alternative B-link, optimistic/versioned, latch-coupled, and copy-on-write designs remain distinct.
Audited atomic, durable, safe, correct, complete, proof, guarantee, minimum, current, and always language for scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Search correctness through a delayed parent update depends on the stated high-key/right-link publication and recovery assumptions.

evidence: The standard-library stable mutation model executed successfully through the repository snippet verifier.
An independently coded trace reproduced the insert, merge, redistribution, separator-repair, and root-shrink states.
Seven online primary/official destinations were retrieved; two intended publisher destinations returned automated-access HTTP 403 and are recorded as such.
Performance statements are framed as mechanisms, possible trade-offs, or measurements to collect rather than benchmark results.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS, disk page, MVCC history, WAL recovery, concurrent schedule, page reclamation, or workload benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives insertion and deletion from the declared comparator/separator representation while separating abstract map semantics, stable structure, operational concurrency/recovery, and maintenance policy.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed byte capacity, pivot truncation, duplicates, uniqueness/visibility, latch/restart ordering, B-link publication, WAL and incomplete repair, deferred deletion/reclamation, hot edges, observability, and crash/concurrency test design.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, bounded executable trace, ten non-duplicative examples, and five exercises progress from stable mutation tracing through production recovery, maintenance policy, and adversarial validation.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a DBMS implementation, comparator/collation, MVCC visibility rule, latch/lock schedule, WAL/recovery path, page reclamation mechanism, storage guarantee, workload result, or production fitness.
